questions.q: Which part of a notebook is the best candidate to move into a module?
options: The narrative Markdown explaining the story
Cleaning logic you would want to rerun or test
A one-off chart used only in the presentation
The title cell
questions.explain: Anything you would run twice or test belongs in functions in a module. Exploration, charts, and commentary are what the notebook is for.

questions.q: What does the line if __name__ == "__main__": do in a script?
options: It makes the script run faster
It imports pandas automatically
It runs the code beneath it only when the file is executed directly, not when it is imported
It prevents anyone from importing the file
questions.explain: When a file is imported, __name__ is the module name rather than "__main__", so the guarded code (usually main()) does not run.

questions.q: Why use argparse for the input and output file paths instead of hard-coding them?
options: So the same script can run on different files without editing the code
Because Python cannot read files otherwise
Because argparse encrypts the files
So the script never needs pandas
questions.explain: Command-line arguments make the script reusable and schedulable: change the flags, not the code.

options: Drops duplicate order IDs, then passes the resulting DataFrame into standardize_region
Sorts the data by order_id
Runs standardize_region on the original data and ignores the duplicate step
Raises an error because .pipe is not a pandas method
questions.explain: .pipe(func) passes the DataFrame as the first argument to func, which lets you chain your own functions in readable order.

questions.q: In the sample run, why does the script report reading 5 rows but writing 4?
options: A row was lost when the file was written
The script always drops the last row
Negative revenue rows were removed
One order_id appeared twice, and the duplicate was dropped during cleaning
questions.explain: The raw sample contains order 2 twice. drop_duplicates(subset="order_id") keeps the first, leaving 4 rows.
